summary: Things the room talks about repeatedly become things Nora can look up, and claims about people are refused.
details: Something mentioned as the object of two different claims becomes a thing with a name and every spelling the room has used for it. Mentioned once, it stays a phrase — there is nothing to look up from a thing that appears in one place.

Dates, prices, quantities, times, negations and links never become things, in English or in Chinese. The rule reads the whole phrase rather than its first word, so a name that happens to start with a number, a month or a weekday is not mistaken for a quantity.

A claim whose subject is somebody in the room is refused outright and counted, matching on their name as the room writes it and not only on an internal identifier. Facts about people belong to a different part of her memory.
limitations: A counted thing like 'five gourds' is not refused. Telling it apart from a real name would need to know which words are nouns; instead it simply never becomes anything unless it turns up twice, which quantities do not.
